title: Bulk Grading (2026)
verdict: Bulk grading for trading cards is cheapest at GMA and CGC and most complete at AGS, where $15 a card from 30 cards includes eight subgrades and a scan report.

CGC and GMA are cheaper on low-value bulk: $10 a card at CGC from 10 cards, if each card is worth $500 or less, and $9 to $12 at GMA from 25 cards. PSA's bulk tier is $24.99 and members only. Choose AGS when you want a report on every card and no value cap.

sections.h: Before you send a bulk order
list: Sort by value first. Cards above a grader's value cap will be moved to a pricier tier.
Pull anything with obvious damage unless you want it slabbed for protection.
List every card accurately on the form. CGC charges $5 for cards that are not fully described.
Pack in rows of sleeved cards in card savers, in the same order as the form.

why: Thirty cards gets you the bulk rate. The report, the subgrades and the slab are the same as on a single-card order, so a shop can list every card with its scan attached.

The wait is short because the grading step is short. AGS lists 20 business days or less on its standard service, 10 and 5 business days on the faster tiers, and same-day grading on request for urgent cards.

Every slab comes with the evidence. The digital report shows eight subgrades, centering data, high-resolution images and a color-coded heightmap of the surface, red on major flaws and green on clean areas. You can download it or share it by link, and the scan stays on file against the cert number.

faq.a: A bulk order is one submission of many cards at a lower per-card rate. AGS starts at 30 cards, CGC at 10 and GMA at 25.

faq.q: How many cards count as a bulk order?
faq.a: 30 at AGS. CGC's bulk tier starts at 10 cards, GMA's economy tier at 25, and GMA drops its price again at 100.

faq.q: Is there a minimum number of cards?
faq.a: Not at AGS. You can send one card at $18, and bulk pricing needs 30. CGC's bulk tier needs 10 cards, ISA needs 10, and GMA needs 10 to 25 depending on the tier.

faq.q: How do I submit cards to AGS?
faq.a: Create an account at agscard.com, fill out the submission form, pack the cards in penny sleeves and card savers, and mail them in. You can also drop off at select AGS locations. The dashboard tracks the order.

faq.q: How should I pack cards for grading?
faq.a: Put each card in a new penny sleeve, then a semi-rigid card saver. Sandwich the stack between cardboard, wrap it in bubble wrap and box it. Top loaders are allowed, but card savers travel better.
